sentences.text: Papiliovenator uniquely possessed a short, subtriangular snout similar to Early Cretaceous troodontids like Mei long, differing from the long snouts of Late Cretaceous relatives.
Fossils of Papiliovenator were found in the Bayan Mandahu Formation of Inner Mongolia, China.
Unique skeletal traits of Papiliovenator suggest a high diversity of troodontid body forms in the Late Cretaceous Gobi Desert.
The only known species in the genus is Papiliovenator neimengguensis.
Papiliovenator is classified within the family Troodontidae.
Researchers classify Papiliovenator as the earliest-diverging member of a clade containing all Late Cretaceous troodontids, excluding Almas ukhaa.
Papiliovenator lived during the Late Cretaceous, approximately between 83 and 72 million years ago in the Campanian stage.
